generate.title: Collect your answers
generate.goal: Get real answers from your own prompt, saved as files, before you build anything.
why: One answer proves little, because the model varies from run to run. A baseline is a pass rate across several runs, not one answer.
Prompt, then answer, then file, then checker, then verdict. Every arrow is a deliberate action. Nothing moves on by itself.
This course uses a blind folder that holds only your prompt, so the model cannot read your tests. A model that can read them quietly writes to them, and your baseline would look better than it is.
Each run is a new chat, so no run can remember an earlier one. Five runs is what this course uses, because it gives a steady rate without taking long.
The app starts your AI on an everyday model and records its name for you. A score belongs to one prompt on one model, and a good prompt should not need the most powerful model.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches work too, and scripts, testing-tool configuration files and written test cases are all fine ways to evaluate.
instructions: Your AI window opens by itself the first time you open this step. It opens in the blind folder, which holds only your prompt. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.

The app starts your AI on the model chosen with the Sonnet / Haiku switch above the AI window (Sonnet unless you changed it) and records that model for you. Sonnet is the everyday default and Haiku is the lighter, faster one. The most capable flagship models, such as Opus, are not offered, because this course compares prompts, not models. A change to the switch applies the next time your AI starts.
If your AI asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No. If your AI exits, press Open a new AI chat.
Depending on its settings, your AI may ask for approvals or may act on its own. Any approval requests appear in the terminal, and you answer them there. The app never answers for you.
Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. Do not add anything.
The app waits for output.txt, saves it as your run file and closes your AI window.
For each of runs 2 to 5, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again. One prompt, one answer, one new chat each time. No second tries and no edits.
generate.line: Read prompt.md, follow it, and save only your answer to output.txt. Do nothing else.

promptfoo.title: Build the config
promptfoo.goal: Have your agent build the promptfoo config from your test cases, then see the config score one real answer.
why: You decide what good means. The agent writes the config. Your job is to check that the config means what you meant.

A config is your criteria written as rules that promptfoo applies the same way every time. The echo provider hands each saved answer to the checks unchanged, so no AI model is used and no API key is needed.
This course has the agent follow a skill, a plain-text instruction file that says exactly how to do the job. You can read it and hold the agent to it. There is nothing to install.
The first look is not the baseline. You see the loop work once before you are asked to doubt it. The baseline comes after your thresholds are settled.
The config sees only the saved answers. It never sees your prompt or your notes.
instructions: Your AI window opens by itself when you open this step, in your project folder. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.
If your AI asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No. If your AI exits, press Open a new AI chat.

Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. It reads the skill and builds promptfooconfig.yaml, with one test for each of your five runs. If your AI asks for approvals, they appear in the terminal.

Read the NOT CHECKED list. Those criteria are not covered. Rewrite a threshold in test-cases.md with a number, a list of terms you choose, or a label, then ask your AI to update the config. Spend at most 3 minutes, or leave it and move on.
Read the Interpretation choices. They are decisions the agent made for you, such as whole word or part of a word. Agree, or change test-cases.md.
Press Run first look. The app runs the whole config with promptfoo, which takes a few seconds, and shows you the result for your first run. You will see PASS, FAIL or NOT CHECKED for each criterion.
A non-zero exit code is normal. It only means at least one criterion failed or is NOT CHECKED. If promptfoo itself shows every test as failed while a criterion is NOT CHECKED, that is expected too.
Tick both boxes, then press Check my work.
promptfoo.line: Read skills/build-promptfoo-config/SKILL.md and follow it in build mode on test-cases.md. Add runs/run-1.txt to runs/run-5.txt as tests named run-1 to run-5.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent cannot read the skill file.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the text of SKILL.md into the terminal and add "Follow these instructions" before the line.

troubleshooting.problem: The config has an error.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the error into the terminal and ask your AI to fix it without changing any threshold. Then press Run first look again.

troubleshooting.problem: A label check fails on an output that looks right.
troubleshooting.fix: Files written on Windows end each line with two hidden characters, a carriage return and a line feed (\r\n), and a check that looks for a label at the end of a line can miss it. Tell your AI in the terminal: "Allow for \r\n line endings in the label checks. Do not change any threshold." Then press Run first look again.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent adds an llm-rubric check or asks for an API key.
troubleshooting.fix: Say no. The checks must be rules only, and no API key is needed. The scan will stop you until the check is gone.

troubleshooting.problem: The first look is slow.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait. The app runs the copy of promptfoo it already downloaded, so a run normally takes a few seconds. If it takes more than 10 minutes, the app stops it and tells you.

troubleshooting.problem: Every test shows as failed.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. A NOT CHECKED criterion is built to fail on purpose, so promptfoo marks every test as failed. The app shows each criterion on its own, so you can still see which ones passed.

troubleshooting.problem: The exit code is not 0.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal. promptfoo exits with a non-zero code whenever any criterion fails or is NOT CHECKED.

troubleshooting.problem: Many criteria are NOT CHECKED.
troubleshooting.fix: Spend at most 3 minutes on rewrites. A criterion that stays NOT CHECKED is counted as not covered. Do not loosen it just to get a pass.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI reports a temporary error.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the terminal.

fixtures.title: Make fixtures

why: A checker needs its own test. A bad output must fail, and a polished-but-wrong output must fail.
The fixtures are written without seeing the config, so they test what you asked for, not what the config happens to do.
This course uses a new chat in a folder with only your test cases, your prompt and one skill, so it cannot open promptfooconfig.yaml or your runs.
The answer key comes later, after you lock your predictions, so nothing can influence them. A prediction is only useful if you commit to it first.

why: Commit before seeing results. Prediction shows where your idea of the code differs from the code.
Once locked, your predictions cannot change. That keeps the comparison honest.
The answer key does not exist yet. It is written after you lock, so nothing can influence your predictions.
instructions: Read the polished fixture below.
For each criterion, pick P for pass, F for fail, or NC for NOT CHECKED, for both fixtures.
Answer three questions. What is wrong with the polished fixture? Which of your criteria should catch that? Across your five runs, which criterion will fail most often?
Press Lock. You cannot change your predictions after that.

troubleshooting.problem: No criteria appear in the grid.
troubleshooting.fix: The app could not read the criteria in your test-cases.md. Add one row for each criterion yourself.

troubleshooting.problem: You want to change a prediction after locking.
troubleshooting.fix: You cannot. A locked prediction is what you compare against, and a wrong guess is useful.

key.title: Write the answer key

why: The key is written only after you lock, so it cannot influence your predictions, even if your AI shows it on screen.
This is a new chat in a folder with only your test cases, your prompt, one skill and the two fixtures. It cannot open promptfooconfig.yaml or your runs.
The key judges each fixture against your requirements, not against what the config happens to do.

key.goal: Now that your predictions are locked, have a new chat write the answer key for your two fixtures.
why: The key is written only after you lock, so it cannot influence your predictions, even if your AI shows it on screen.
This is a new chat in a folder with only your test cases, your prompt, one skill and the two fixtures. It cannot open check.py or your runs.
The key judges each fixture against your requirements, not against what the checker happens to do.
instructions: Your AI window opens by itself when you open this step, in the answer key folder. It is a new chat. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.
If your AI asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No. If your AI exits, press Open a new AI chat.

Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. If your AI asks for approvals, they appear in the terminal. A long approval request may not fit, so scroll up to read all of it before you answer.
Your AI may show the key as it writes it. That is fine now, because your predictions are locked.
Press Check my work. The app seals the key away from your project folder. You will read it in the next step, after the checker has run.
key.line: Read skills/make-eval-fixtures/SKILL.md. The two fixture files are already in fixtures/. Do not change them. Follow only the Answer key section, using test-cases.md, and write fixtures/answer-key.md. Do nothing else.
key.folder_label: Answer key folder (test cases, prompt, one skill and the two fixtures only)

troubleshooting.fix: Paste the text of SKILL.md into the terminal and add "Follow these instructions" before the line.

troubleshooting.fix: Press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again. The app restores both fixtures when the window opens.

troubleshooting.problem: The file is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Look at the terminal. If your AI is set to ask for approval, it may be waiting for you. Answer it there, then press Check my work again.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI reports a temporary error.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the terminal.

run.title: Run it

ui.run_blurb: This runs check.py on both fixtures: the bad one and the polished one.

promptfoo.goal: Run your config on both fixtures and compare the result with your predictions.
why: The same file always gives the same verdict. The AI that wrote the output varies. The config does not.
Every surprise is either a vague threshold, a config that reads your threshold differently, or a wrong guess. Which one it is tells you what to fix.
If the polished fixture passes every criterion, you found a check that was window dressing.

If promptfoo shows every test as failed, that is expected while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. A NOT CHECKED criterion is built to fail on purpose, so promptfoo marks every test as failed. The app shows each criterion on its own.
instructions: Press Run checker. The app runs your config on both fixtures with promptfoo. No AI is involved, and it takes a few seconds.
A non-zero exit code is normal. It only means at least one criterion failed or is NOT CHECKED.
The grid compares your predictions with the config. Surprises are marked.
Read the answer key. It opens after your run succeeds.
Classify each surprise: the threshold is vague or too loose, the config reads my threshold differently than I meant, or I predicted wrong.
Press Check my work.

troubleshooting.problem: The exit code is not 0.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal. promptfoo exits with a non-zero code whenever any criterion fails or is NOT CHECKED.

troubleshooting.problem: Every test shows as failed.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. That criterion fails on purpose in every test, so promptfoo marks every test as failed. Look at the grid: it shows each criterion on its own, and the other criteria still pass or fail on their merits.

troubleshooting.problem: The run reports an error.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the message and the raw output. promptfooconfig.yaml may have an error. Go back to your AI and ask it to fix the error without changing any threshold.

troubleshooting.problem: A label check fails on a fixture that looks right.
troubleshooting.fix: Files written on Windows end each line with two hidden characters, a carriage return and a line feed (\r\n), and a check that looks for a label at the end of a line can miss it. If it is a surprise, classify it as the config reading your threshold differently than you meant. In the next step, add a short note to that criterion in test-cases.md             saying that a Windows line ending after the label is fine. Then open that step, paste its line into your AI window, and tell your AI in the terminal: "Allow for \r\n line endings in the label checks. Do not change any threshold."

troubleshooting.problem: The run takes a long time.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait. A run normally takes a few seconds. If it takes more than 10 minutes, the app stops it and says so. Then press Run checker again.

troubleshooting.problem: The polished fixture passed everything.
troubleshooting.fix: Good: you found a gap. Read the answer key, then fix the threshold that should catch it in the next step.

fix.title: Fix the spec

ui.edit_blurb: Fix the spec, not the checker. Reword the threshold here, save, then copy the line below and paste it into your AI window so your AI updates check.py to match.

promptfoo.goal: Fix the spec, not the config. Change a threshold in your test cases, and let the agent update the config to match.
why: When a result is wrong, change the written rules and let the agent update the config to match, so the two never drift apart.
Never edit the config to make a result pass, because a failing result is the information.
Deterministic checks narrow the gap. They do not close it. A tightened keyword check is still a proxy.
instructions: Read the reason on each surprise. If the bad fixture passes something it should fail, the threshold is too loose. If the polished fixture passes everything, tighten the threshold that should catch what it gets wrong.
Edit test-cases.md here and save it. Change the wording of the threshold.
Your AI window opens by itself when you open this step, in your project folder. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.
Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. It updates only the assertions whose threshold changed.
A long approval request may not fit in the terminal. Scroll up to read all of it before you answer.
Press Run both fixtures. The bad fixture should fail more than half of its checked criteria.
The polished fixture should fail at least one criterion. If you think it should pass, write why in the box.
Press Check my work. If there were no surprises and the polished fixture already failed a criterion, you can skip this step.
promptfoo.line: I changed test-cases.md. Update promptfooconfig.yaml to match, changing only the assertions whose threshold changed. Then run the two fixtures again.

troubleshooting.fix: Change the sentence in test-cases.md instead, then ask your AI to update promptfooconfig.yaml.

troubleshooting.fix: Paste the error into the terminal and ask your AI to fix it without changing any threshold. Then press Run both fixtures again.

troubleshooting.fix: Files written on Windows end each line with two hidden characters, a carriage return and a line feed (\r\n), and a check that looks for a label at the end of a line can miss it. Tell your AI in the terminal: "Allow for \r\n line endings in the label checks. Do not change any threshold." Then press Run both fixtures again.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent added an llm-rubric check or an AI model.
troubleshooting.fix: Say no. The checks must be rules only. The scan will stop you until it is gone.

troubleshooting.problem: The bad fixture no longer fails most criteria.
troubleshooting.fix: The change made a threshold too loose. Tighten it in test-cases.md and run both fixtures again.

troubleshooting.fix: That is normal while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. That criterion fails on purpose in every test. The app shows each criterion on its own.

troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the terminal.

baseline.title: Log your baseline

ui.count_blurb: The app runs your checker on all five runs itself, with no AI. This is the number your log must match.
ui.no_checker: There is no check.py to run.
ui.stale: check.py or one of your runs changed after this count. Press Run my checker on the five runs again.

why: The baseline is the starting number for the next iteration. In Part 4 you change the prompt, run the same config, and compare the new numbers with these.
It is a pass rate across five runs, not one answer, because the model varies from run to run. For example, 4 of 5 is 80%.

It is logged only after your thresholds are settled. If a threshold changes later, the logged numbers used the earlier wording, so they no longer mean the same thing. That is why the first look was never your baseline.
NOT CHECKED means not covered. A NOT CHECKED criterion stays in the log, marked as not checked, and is left out of the overall total. It is a gap to be honest about, not a pass.

Never edit the config to make a failing output pass. A failing result is the information. If a result looks wrong, change the threshold in test-cases.md and let your AI update promptfooconfig.yaml to match.
The app runs your config on the five runs itself, with promptfoo and no AI, and compares its numbers with your log. Your AI writes the log. The app only reads it and never changes it.
instructions: The line you paste names the model your AI used for your five runs. The app recorded it when it started your AI.

Your AI window opens by itself when you open this step, in your project folder. If it asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.

Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. It runs your config on your five runs and adds an Iteration 0 entry to iteration-log.md. Any approval requests appear in the terminal, and you answer them there.

Press Run my checker on the five runs. The app runs your promptfoo config itself and shows the pass rate for each criterion. A non-zero exit code is normal. It only means at least one check failed or is NOT CHECKED.

Compare the app's count with the entry your AI wrote. The numbers should be the same. If your AI logged a different number, say so in the terminal and ask it to correct the entry, or fix the number yourself in iteration-log.md. The app never edits your log.
Press Check my work.

Before Part 4, keep your whole project folder. Look at your five runs and pick the one you think is best. It becomes your known-good output, and your checks should score it 95% or more. If they do not, that tells you something about the config, not the prompt.
Optional: name the criterion that failed most often in your baseline and write one guess why. It becomes your hypothesis in Part 4.
promptfoo.line_template: Read skills/build-promptfoo-config/SKILL.md and follow it in run + log mode. The runs are the tests named run-1 to run-5. The prompt file is prompt-v0.md. The model was {model}.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI cannot read the skill file.
troubleshooting.fix: Open skills{sep}build-promptfoo-config{sep}SKILL.md in your project folder and copy all of its text.             Paste it into the terminal, add the words Follow these instructions, and press Enter.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says promptfoo is not downloaded.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Settings, go to the Setup group, press Install for promptfoo, and choose Check everything again. Then press Run my checker on the five runs.

troubleshooting.problem: The config has an error.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the error into the terminal and ask your AI to fix it without changing any threshold. Then press Run my checker on the five runs again.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI wants an llm-rubric check or an API key.
troubleshooting.fix: Say no. The checks must be rules only, and no API key is needed. The scan will stop the app's own run until the check is gone.

troubleshooting.problem: Every test shows as failed.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. That criterion fails on purpose in every test, so promptfoo marks every test as failed. The app counts each criterion on its own, so the other criteria still show their real pass rates.

troubleshooting.problem: The exit code is not 0.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal. promptfoo exits with a non-zero code whenever any criterion fails or is NOT CHECKED.

troubleshooting.problem: The app's count and your log disagree.
troubleshooting.fix: The app's count comes from running your config itself, so trust it over the log. Ask your AI to correct the entry, or fix the number in iteration-log.md. Do not change promptfooconfig.yaml to match the log.

troubleshooting.problem: You changed a threshold after you logged.
troubleshooting.fix: The logged numbers used the earlier wording. Ask your AI to update promptfooconfig.yaml, press Run my checker on the five runs again, then ask your AI to log again and choose to replace Iteration 0, so the log holds one entry that matches.

troubleshooting.problem: The log has two Iteration 0 entries.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep one. Open iteration-log.md, delete the older entry, and press Check my work again.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI logged a pass rate for a NOT CHECKED criterion.
troubleshooting.fix: A criterion that was not scored cannot have a rate. Ask your AI to list it under Not checked, and write not checked in its table row.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI logged the fixtures or the example files.
troubleshooting.fix: Only your five runs belong in the baseline. Ask your AI to log only the tests named run-1 to run-5.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI reports a temporary error.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the terminal. If it keeps failing, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again.

live.title: Optional: live mode
live.goal: Optional. Have promptfoo write fresh outputs through your own signed-in AI tool, and score them with the same checks. You can skip this step: the course is complete without it.
why: Your five saved runs are fixed. In live mode your AI writes new answers on demand, so you can see how the same checks score answers you have not seen yet.
Each live run is a new answer, so the scores change from run to run. They are a sample, not a baseline.
Live mode never replaces your baseline. It does not use your saved runs, and your promptfooconfig.yaml and iteration-log.md stay exactly as they are.
The checks stay rules only. The AI writes the outputs, and it never grades them. No API key is involved: your AI signs in with its own login.
instructions: Read the warning below. It says what live mode does to your AI, including which AI tool the helper script puts into auto mode.
Tick the box to say you have read it, then choose the AI tool you use. Live mode supports only the AI tools in the list.
The line you paste names the model your AI used for your five runs. The app recorded it when it started your AI.

Press Open a new AI chat. This step never opens your AI window by itself. When your AI is ready for a message, press Copy above the AI window, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. Your AI copies agent-provider.js next to your config, writes promptfooconfig.live.yaml with the same checks, and runs it. Any approval requests appear in the terminal, and you answer them there. The app never answers for you.
Do not ask your AI to log these runs. Your baseline stays the one from your saved runs.
Press Check my work. The app only reads your files. It does not run the live config.
Read the live scores as your AI shows them. They can differ from run to run, and that is expected.

ui.warning_title: Read this before you start live mode
ui.warning_intro: Live mode is optional. The course is complete without it, so you can skip this step.
warning_points: Live mode makes promptfoo call your own signed-in AI tool to write fresh outputs. No API key is involved: your AI uses its own sign-in.

To do that, the helper script agent-provider.js starts your AI by itself. For Devin CLI the helper adds --permission-mode auto, which turns on Devin's auto mode for that run, so Devin may act without asking you. For GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code the helper adds no permission flag.
The helper runs your AI from an empty temporary folder, so it cannot see test-cases.md or your other project files.
Results change from run to run, because every live run is a new answer.
Live mode does not use your saved runs and never changes your baseline. Your promptfooconfig.yaml and iteration-log.md must stay exactly as they are.
The app does not run live mode. Your own AI runs it in the AI window, and you answer any approval requests there.
ui.ack_label: I have read this warning. I understand that live mode starts my AI by itself, and that for Devin CLI the helper turns on auto mode so it may act without asking me.
ui.cli_hint: Live mode supports these three. Choose the one you use, so the line names it.

ui.started_note: The app noted your promptfooconfig.yaml and iteration-log.md when you started. Check my work confirms that neither one changed.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent cannot read the skill file.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the text of SKILL.md into the terminal and add "Follow these instructions" before the line.

troubleshooting.problem: Live mode says "Not logged in" or "No agent found".
troubleshooting.fix: Choose the AI tool you really use in the list above, and paste the line into your AI window again. The helper starts that AI tool by its short name, so the name must work in a normal terminal. If it says Not logged in, sign in to that AI tool once in a normal terminal, then paste the line again.

troubleshooting.problem: The agent adds an llm-rubric check or asks for an API key.
troubleshooting.fix: Say no. The checks must be rules only, and live mode needs no API key. The scan will stop you until the check is gone.

troubleshooting.problem: Every test shows as failed.
troubleshooting.fix: That is normal while any criterion is NOT CHECKED. That criterion fails on purpose in every test, so promptfoo marks every test as failed. The summary shows each criterion on its own.

troubleshooting.problem: The live scores are different each time.
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected. Every live run is a new answer, so the scores change. They are a sample and never replace your baseline.

troubleshooting.problem: The config has an error.
troubleshooting.fix: Paste the error into the terminal and ask your AI to fix it without changing any threshold. Then ask it to run the live config again.

troubleshooting.problem: Your prompt file contains double curly brackets.
troubleshooting.fix: promptfoo reads {{ and {% as template syntax, so it may change those parts of your prompt before your AI sees them. Ask your AI in the terminal to show you where they are, and keep that in mind when you read the live scores. Your prompt file stays as it is.

troubleshooting.problem: Check my work says promptfooconfig.yaml or iteration-log.md changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Live mode must not change them. Ask your AI to undo that change, or restore the file yourself, then press Check my work again. Your baseline stays as it was.

troubleshooting.problem: Check my work says agent-provider.js is not the copy that came with the course.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your AI to copy agent-provider.js again from skills{sep}build-promptfoo-config next to your config, without editing it. Then press Check my work again.

troubleshooting.problem: Your AI reports a temporary error.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the terminal. If it keeps failing, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again.
